dsa.title: Two Sum
dsa.statement: Given an array of integers and a target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target. Assume exactly one solution, and do not reuse an element.
hints: Nudge: for each number, what other number would complete the target?
Approach: remember numbers you have already seen and what you still need, so each lookup is fast instead of scanning the whole array again.
Pseudocode: seen = empty map; for each index i and value v: need = target - v; if need in seen, return [seen[need], i]; else store v at i.

dsa.title: Valid Parentheses
dsa.statement: Given a string of brackets ()[]{} , decide whether it is valid: every opening bracket must be closed by the same type, in the correct order.
hints: Nudge: which bracket did you see most recently, and what must come next?
Approach: track opening brackets in order, and match each closing bracket against the most recent unmatched one.
Pseudocode: stack = empty; for each character: if opening, push it; else if stack empty or top does not match, return false; else pop. Valid if stack is empty at the end.

dsa.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
dsa.statement: Given daily prices, choose one day to buy and a later day to sell to maximise profit. Return the maximum profit, or 0 if no profit is possible.
hints: Nudge: you only need the lowest price seen so far, not every pair of days.
Approach: walk once, remembering the cheapest buy price and the best profit available at each step.
Pseudocode: min_price = infinity; best = 0; for each price: min_price = min(min_price, price); best = max(best, price - min_price).

dsa.title: Reverse a String In Place
dsa.statement: Reverse a list of characters in place, using only constant extra space.
hints: Nudge: which two positions would you swap first?
Approach: work from both ends towards the middle, swapping as you go.
Pseudocode: left = 0; right = last index; while left < right: swap s[left] and s[right]; left += 1; right -= 1.

dsa.title: Valid Anagram
dsa.statement: Given two strings, decide whether one is an anagram of the other: same letters, same counts, possibly different order.
hints: Nudge: what has to match — the letters, or something about them?
Approach: count how many times each letter appears in each string, then compare the counts.
Pseudocode: if lengths differ, return false; count letters in s; subtract counts for letters in t; valid if every count is zero.

dsa.title: Contains Duplicate
dsa.statement: Given an integer array, return true if any value appears at least twice, and false otherwise.
hints: Nudge: what do you need to remember as you scan?
Approach: keep a set of values seen so far; a repeat means an immediate answer.
Pseudocode: seen = empty set; for each value: if value in seen, return true; add value to seen. Return false.

dsa.title: Move Zeroes
dsa.statement: Move all zeroes in an array to the end, keeping the relative order of the non-zero elements, in place.
hints: Nudge: one pointer can mark where the next non-zero element belongs.
Approach: sweep once, placing non-zeroes at the front in order, then fill the rest with zeroes.
Pseudocode: place = 0; for each value: if value != 0: nums[place] = value; place += 1; then fill nums[place:] with 0.

dsa.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
dsa.statement: Given a string, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
hints: Nudge: when a character repeats, what part of your current window is still usable?
Approach: slide a window across the string, remembering where each character was last seen, and shrink from the left past any repeat.
Pseudocode: left = 0; best = 0; last_seen = map; for right, ch in string: if ch seen at or after left, left = last_seen[ch] + 1; record ch at right; best = max(best, right - left + 1).
